relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Entity A directly owns or controls Entity B based on declared ownership or legal hierarchy.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Customer Master; Legal Entity Master; KYC / Onboarding; UBO Repository
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Company registries; GLEIF; Orbis; Dun & Bradstreet; Refinitiv; S&P Capital IQ
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Legal Entity ID; LEI; ownership %; voting rights; effective dates; control indicator
relationships.Regulatory / Risk Relevance: Economic group consolidation; large exposure; related-party assessment
relationships.Implementation Notes: Direct ownership and legal control rules should be aligned to bank policy and applicable regulation.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: A natural person or legal entity ultimately owns or controls the counterparty through one or more ownership layers.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: KYC; AML; Client Onboarding; UBO Repository; Customer Master
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Company registries; Orbis; Refinitiv; S&P Capital IQ; national UBO registers where accessible
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: UBO ID; ownership %; voting rights; control type; ownership path; declaration date
relationships.Regulatory / Risk Relevance: Related-party lending; AML; group risk; concentration
relationships.Data Refresh: Event-driven on KYC change; periodic refresh
relationships.Implementation Notes: Retain the full path, not only the final UBO link.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Two or more entities share the same material shareholder or controlling investor.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: KYC; UBO Repository; Customer Master; Legal Entity Master
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Orbis; Refinitiv; S&P Capital IQ; company registries; SEC / exchange filings
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Shareholder ID; holding %; voting %; instrument class; effective date
relationships.Regulatory / Risk Relevance: Hidden concentration; common control; related parties
relationships.Implementation Notes: A common shareholder does not always establish a regulatory connected group without control or economic interdependence.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Two entities have a shared director, officer or key management person.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: KYC; CRM; Customer Master; Legal Entity Master
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: BoardEx; Companies House; SEC filings; company registries; annual reports
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Person ID; role; appointment and resignation dates; board type
relationships.Regulatory / Risk Relevance: Related-party screening; governance linkage; hidden control
relationships.Implementation Notes: Use as strong evidence of linkage, but not automatically as proof of common control.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Entities are assigned to a formal group under bank policy or regulatory grouping rules.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Customer Master; Group Management; Credit Risk Mart; Limit Management; Regulatory Reporting
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: External corporate hierarchy data as corroboration
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Group ID; group type; rationale; approval; effective date; reviewer
relationships.Regulatory / Risk Relevance: Group exposure aggregation; risk appetite; limits; reporting
relationships.Implementation Notes: Support multiple group views, for example economic, borrower and regulatory.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: A guarantor provides contractual support to a borrower or facility.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Loan Origination; Facility Management; Guarantee System; Trade Finance; Credit Administration
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Public filings or registries where guarantees are disclosed
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Guarantor ID; beneficiary; facility ID; guarantee amount; currency; coverage; expiry
relationships.Regulatory / Risk Relevance: Connected exposure; credit mitigation; dependency analysis
relationships.Implementation Notes: Model guarantee-to-facility and facility-to-borrower links to avoid ambiguity.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Two or more group entities guarantee each other or common obligations.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Facility Management; Guarantee System; Loan Documentation; Credit Memos
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Public debt documents; company filings where available
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Guarantee chain; amount; seniority; coverage; effective date
relationships.Regulatory / Risk Relevance: Default correlation; group dependency; concentration
relationships.Implementation Notes: Potentially strong evidence of economic interdependence, subject to legal review.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: The same collateral asset or provider supports exposures of multiple borrowers or facilities.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Collateral Management; Loan Origination; Security Perfection; Valuation System
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Land/property registries; lien registries; securities depositories where accessible
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Collateral ID; owner; provider; secured facilities; valuation; lien priority; jurisdiction
relationships.Regulatory / Risk Relevance: Double counting risk; concentration; recovery dependency
relationships.Implementation Notes: Separate collateral owner, provider, asset and security-interest concepts.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Entities are linked through a legally documented joint venture, associate or affiliate structure.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Customer Master; KYC; Legal Entity Master; Credit File
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Company registries; annual reports; Capital IQ; Orbis
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Ownership %; control rights; JV agreement; consolidation treatment
relationships.Regulatory / Risk Relevance: Group structure; concentration; strategic dependency
relationships.Implementation Notes: Store relationship subtype and bilateral/equity details.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Multiple lenders and one or more obligors participate in a syndicated facility.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Syndicated Loan System; Loan Servicing; Facility Management; Treasury
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Refinitiv LPC; Dealogic; Bloomberg; public debt disclosures
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Facility ID; role; borrower; lender; commitment; drawn amount; agent; maturity
relationships.Regulatory / Risk Relevance: Shared borrower; cross-bank exposure; concentration
relationships.Implementation Notes: Model participants and obligors separately.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: A branch is legally linked to a head office or legal entity.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Customer Master; Legal Entity Master; KYC; Finance hierarchy
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: GLEIF; company or banking registries
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Branch ID; head office ID; country; legal status; effective date
relationships.Regulatory / Risk Relevance: Jurisdictional exposure; legal entity aggregation
relationships.Implementation Notes: Useful for legal and country exposure views.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Entity A supplies goods or services to Entity B; strength can be measured by spend, invoices, trade flows or disclosed dependency.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Supply Chain Finance; Trade Finance; Accounts Payable; Payments / Cash Management; Procurement; borrower financial statements; CRM
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: FactSet Revere; Bloomberg Supply Chain; S&P Panjiva; ImportGenius; Dun & Bradstreet; company filings
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Supplier / buyer ID; invoice value; payment volume; purchase share; product; country; start/end date
relationships.Regulatory / Risk Relevance: Operational dependency; indirect credit risk; contagion
relationships.Data Refresh: Monthly / daily where transaction data is available
relationships.Implementation Notes: Inferred relationship should retain calculation window and confidence.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: A borrower derives revenue or receivables from a customer or off-taker.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Receivables; Cash Management; borrower ERP feeds; financial statements; credit reviews; trade finance
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Annual reports; regulatory filings; FactSet Revere; Bloomberg Supply Chain; industry research
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Customer ID; revenue share; receivable balance; concentration %; contract term
relationships.Regulatory / Risk Relevance: Revenue concentration; EWI; contagion
relationships.Implementation Notes: Materiality thresholds should be configurable by sector.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Supply or customer dependencies extend beyond direct Tier 1 counterparties.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Trade Finance; SCF; payments; procurement; borrower disclosures
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Panjiva; ImportGenius; FactSet Revere; Bloomberg Supply Chain; D&B
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Relationship tier; product; shipment/trade volume; dependency share; route
relationships.Regulatory / Risk Relevance: Propagation analysis; sector and operational stress
relationships.Implementation Notes: Use path depth limits and explain the evidence for each edge.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Multiple borrowers depend on the same lender, investor, fund or refinancing market.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Treasury; Syndicated Lending; Debt Management; Securities / Issuance records; KYC
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Refinitiv LPC; Dealogic; Bloomberg; Capital IQ; public debt filings
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Provider ID; facility/security ID; commitment; maturity; refinancing date; amount
relationships.Regulatory / Risk Relevance: Funding concentration; refinance contagion
relationships.Implementation Notes: Relevant for ecosystem stress even where the bank has no direct exposure to the provider.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Entities share a private equity sponsor, sovereign investor, family office or investment fund.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: KYC; UBO; CRM; Customer Master; investment banking records
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: PitchBook; Preqin; Capital IQ; Refinitiv; Orbis; company filings
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Sponsor ID; ownership %; fund; investment date; board rights; exit status
relationships.Regulatory / Risk Relevance: Common control; correlated strategy; funding dependency
relationships.Implementation Notes: May become Level 1 where control criteria are satisfied.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: A sustained material payment flow exists between counterparties.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Payments; Current Accounts; Cash Management; SWIFT messages; Transaction Monitoring
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Generally internal; external payment/network reference data may support entity identification
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Account ID; counterparty account; amount; frequency; purpose code; country; observation period
relationships.Regulatory / Risk Relevance: Economic dependency; emerging customer/supplier link; EWI
relationships.Implementation Notes: Behavioral evidence requires legal, privacy and model-governance review.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Entities share or depend on a treasury, derivatives, securities-finance or prime-brokerage counterparty.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Treasury; OTC Derivatives; Securities Finance; Prime Brokerage; Collateral; Counterparty Credit Risk
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Bloomberg; Refinitiv; market data; public disclosures
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Counterparty ID; product; notional; current exposure; collateral; maturity
relationships.Regulatory / Risk Relevance: Wrong-way risk; counterparty concentration; market contagion
relationships.Implementation Notes: Aggregate consistently with netting and collateral policy.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Multiple counterparties depend on the same critical service, technology, cloud or outsourcing provider.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Procurement; Vendor Management; Operational Risk; Third-Party Risk; Accounts Payable; contracts
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: D&B; vendor intelligence; public disclosures; regulatory outsourcing registers where accessible
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Vendor ID; service; criticality; spend; geography; contract dates; subcontractor
relationships.Regulatory / Risk Relevance: Operational concentration; business continuity contagion
relationships.Implementation Notes: Use only relevant critical services to avoid noisy connections.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Entities rely on the same insurer, credit insurer or protection provider.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Insurance records; collateral / credit protection; trade credit insurance; procurement
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Public filings; insurer databases; broker-provided data subject to rights
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Provider ID; policy ID; insured risk; coverage; limit; expiry
relationships.Regulatory / Risk Relevance: Risk mitigation concentration; recovery dependency
relationships.Implementation Notes: A shared insurer is an economic dependency, not necessarily a connected-counterparty relationship.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Entities share industry, commodity, technology or infrastructure dependencies.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Customer Master; industry classification; Credit Risk Mart; transaction data
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Moody’s; S&P; Fitch; industry associations; commodity and sector data providers
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Industry code; subsector; commodity; business model; exposure share
relationships.Regulatory / Risk Relevance: Sector concentration; scenario stress; correlation
relationships.Implementation Notes: Use hierarchy depth and material revenue share to control granularity.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Entities share material operating, revenue, supplier, asset or funding dependency on a geography.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Customer Master; KYC; exposure; collateral; payment and trade data; borrower financials
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: IMF; OECD; World Bank; central banks; geographic and country-risk sources
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Country; region; revenue %; assets %; supplier %; exposure %; booking vs risk country
relationships.Regulatory / Risk Relevance: Country concentration; geopolitical / climate / macro stress
relationships.Implementation Notes: Use multiple geographical dimensions rather than one address.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Entities rely on the same port, corridor, vessel, carrier, warehouse or logistics provider.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Trade Finance; shipping documents; bills of lading; procurement; supply-chain finance
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: AIS / maritime data; Panjiva; ImportGenius; shipping data providers; port data
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Port; route; vessel IMO; carrier; bill of lading; shipment volume; commodity
relationships.Regulatory / Risk Relevance: Supply disruption; geographic contagion; trade concentration
relationships.Implementation Notes: Useful for sector-specific PoCs; may not be available bank-wide.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Entities depend on the same energy source, commodity, producer, infrastructure or price factor.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Trade Finance; commodity finance; procurement; borrower financials; collateral
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Commodity exchanges; market data providers; energy statistics; public filings
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Commodity; volume; cost/revenue share; supplier; location; contract type
relationships.Regulatory / Risk Relevance: Commodity concentration; scenario propagation
relationships.Implementation Notes: Requires sector-specific materiality and stress assumptions.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Entities participate in the same project, consortium, concession or long-term contract without common ownership.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Project Finance; Loan Origination; Trade Finance; Credit File; CRM; contracts
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Public procurement portals; company announcements; project databases
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Project ID; role; contract value; duration; sponsor; guarantees
relationships.Regulatory / Risk Relevance: Project concentration; performance contagion
relationships.Implementation Notes: Model the project as a node to support multi-party relationships.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Two entities share the same registered address during overlapping periods.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: KYC; Customer Master; Legal Entity Master; Client Onboarding
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Company registries; Orbis; D&B; SEC / exchange filings
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Normalized address; unit; postcode; country; effective dates
relationships.Implementation Notes: Use only for approved risk purposes; avoid treating shared address alone as conclusive.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Entities share mailing or operating premises.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: CRM; KYC; Customer Master; Site Visit reports
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Company websites; registries; geospatial/business directories
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Address type; geocode; dates; branch/site indicator
relationships.Implementation Notes: Location data may be personal for sole traders; apply access controls.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Entities share a declared contact number.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: KYC; CRM; Onboarding; Customer Master
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Company registries; public corporate websites; directories
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Country code; normalized number; extension; contact type; dates
relationships.Implementation Notes: Contact data is sensitive; restrict and log use.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Entities use the same non-public corporate email domain.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: CRM; KYC; Onboarding; digital channels
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Company websites; domain registration sources where legally available
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Normalized domain; account type; first/last observed
relationships.Implementation Notes: Use only business contact data and approved sources.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: An identical contact email is declared for multiple entities.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: KYC; CRM; Onboarding
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Company filings or websites where disclosed
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Email; role; effective dates
relationships.Implementation Notes: Potential personal data; stronger restrictions and review required.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Entities share or alias the same tax identifier, indicating duplicate or branch records, or a data-quality issue.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Customer Master; KYC; Tax Reporting; Onboarding
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Tax registries only where legally accessible
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Tax ID; country; entity type; validity dates
relationships.Implementation Notes: Highly sensitive identifier; mask and restrict.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: LEI identifiers resolve entity identity and direct/ultimate parent relationships.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Customer Master; Counterparty Master; Treasury
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: GLEIF
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: LEI; legal name; status; direct parent LEI; ultimate parent LEI
relationships.Implementation Notes: Corporate identifier; retain source and status.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Multiple entities transact through or declare the same account.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Payments; Cash Management; Loan Servicing; Trade Finance; KYC
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Generally unavailable externally; SWIFT reference data supports bank identity
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Account token; IBAN; bank; holder; signatory; dates
relationships.Implementation Notes: Highly sensitive; strict purpose limitation, encryption and access logging.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Entities use the same bank or branch for material flows.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Payments; Treasury; Trade Finance
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: SWIFT reference data
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: BIC; bank legal entity; branch; country; flow share
relationships.Implementation Notes: Payment-data usage must be approved.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: The same person is authorized for multiple entities or accounts.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: KYC; Account Opening; Mandate Management; Customer Master
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Company filings where signatories are disclosed
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Person ID; role; authority; account/entity; effective dates
relationships.Implementation Notes: Personal data; role-based access and explainable use.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Entities share a contact person or bank relationship manager.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: CRM; Customer Master
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: None normally required
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Contact person; RM; portfolio; role; dates
relationships.Implementation Notes: Internal personnel data; not a risk linkage by itself.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Entities use the same legal representative, company secretary or counsel.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: KYC; Legal; Procurement; Credit Files; invoices
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Company filings; court filings; public legal records
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Representative ID; role; case/filing; dates
relationships.Implementation Notes: Professional relationship alone is weak evidence.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Entities appoint the same auditor or audit firm.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Financial Statements; Credit File; Procurement
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Annual reports; company filings
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Auditor; audit entity; year; opinion
relationships.Implementation Notes: Public corporate data where available.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: The same property, security or asset identifier appears against multiple facilities.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Collateral Management; Security Perfection; Loan Origination
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Property / lien registries; securities depositories where accessible
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Asset ID; owner; valuation; lien; facility allocation
relationships.Implementation Notes: Property ownership data may require jurisdiction controls.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Multiple business accounts use the same device or network identifier.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Digital Banking; Fraud Monitoring; Cybersecurity logs
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Generally internal; threat intelligence may support risk assessment
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Tokenized device ID; IP; login timestamps; user role
relationships.Implementation Notes: Highly sensitive behavioral data; legal, privacy and cybersecurity approval essential.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Entities share domain registration, hosting or website identifiers.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: CRM; KYC; Digital onboarding
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Domain registration sources and public websites, subject to lawful access
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Domain; registrant organization; nameserver; first/last seen
relationships.Implementation Notes: Respect licensing and privacy restrictions.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: The same guarantor supports multiple obligors or facilities.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Guarantee System; Facility Management; Trade Finance; Credit Administration
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Public filings where disclosed
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Guarantor ID; guarantee amount; beneficiary; expiry
relationships.Implementation Notes: Formal credit-support information.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Multiple entities direct funds to a common beneficiary.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Payments; Trade Finance; Cash Management; Transaction Monitoring
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Sanctions / PEP / corporate registry sources for beneficiary resolution
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Beneficiary token; account; amount; frequency; purpose; country
relationships.Implementation Notes: Sensitive transaction data; strict purpose and access controls.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Entities are linked in credible news, filings, court or regulatory documents.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: News feeds held internally; Legal; Compliance; Credit Research; Analyst Notes
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Reuters; Bloomberg; Factiva; court filings; regulatory releases; company announcements
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Entity mentions; document type; relationship phrase; publication date; source credibility
relationships.Implementation Notes: Observe content licensing and retention rights.

relationships.Relationship Definition / Rule: Entities appear on the same project, contract, concession, procurement award or consortium.
relationships.Internal Data Sources: Project Finance; Trade Finance; CRM; Loan Origination; Credit File
relationships.Probable External Data Sources: Public procurement portals; project databases; company announcements
relationships.Evidence / Key Attributes: Project ID; participant role; contract value; start/end dates
relationships.Implementation Notes: Use public or licensed sources.

sources.Primary Relationship Coverage: Identity; group; address; contact; industry; legal form
sources.Typical Data Captured: Customer ID; legal name; aliases; country; industry; group ID; address; contact
sources.Key Data Quality Controls: Uniqueness; completeness; golden-record survivorship; effective dates

sources.Primary Relationship Coverage: UBO; directors; shareholders; signatories; address; tax ID
sources.Typical Data Captured: Declared ownership; UBO; directors; documents; risk classification
sources.Key Data Quality Controls: Document validity; recency; mandatory fields; source provenance
sources.Licensing / Privacy / Access Considerati: Contains personal and sensitive customer data

sources.Primary Relationship Coverage: Related parties; beneficiaries; transaction networks; sanctions links
sources.Typical Data Captured: Alerts; beneficiaries; counterparties; transaction patterns
sources.Key Data Quality Controls: Entity resolution; alert status; permitted-use controls
sources.Notes: Use subject to policy and legal approval.

sources.Typical Data Captured: LEI; parent; subsidiaries; ownership %; effective dates
sources.Key Data Quality Controls: Hierarchy loops; duplicate entities; temporal consistency

sources.Typical Data Captured: Facility ID; obligor; guarantor; commitment; drawn amount; maturity
sources.Key Data Quality Controls: Facility-obligor mapping; currency; active status; reconciliation

sources.Typical Data Captured: Asset ID; owner; value; lien; secured facilities; location
sources.Key Data Quality Controls: Unique asset; lien priority; valuation recency; allocation

sources.Typical Data Captured: Applicant; beneficiary; issuing/advising bank; amount; goods; country
sources.Key Data Quality Controls: Party mapping; duplicate documents; transaction status
sources.Notes: Strong source for commercial relationship discovery.

sources.Primary Relationship Coverage: Material payment relationship; beneficiary; bank relationship
sources.Typical Data Captured: Payer/payee; accounts; BIC; amount; frequency; purpose
sources.Key Data Quality Controls: Account tokenization; duplicates; reversals; purpose codes

sources.Typical Data Captured: Vendor ID; contract; spend; service; criticality; dates
sources.Key Data Quality Controls: Vendor-group normalization; active contracts; criticality
sources.Notes: More relevant for bank dependencies than borrower dependencies unless borrower data is provided.

sources.Primary Relationship Coverage: Contacts; group view; commercial links; RM knowledge
sources.Typical Data Captured: Contacts; parent; interactions; opportunities; relationship tags
sources.Key Data Quality Controls: Free-text quality; duplicate contacts; stale links

sources.Source / System: Credit Risk Mart / Ratings / Watchlist / Covenants
sources.Primary Relationship Coverage: Risk status; rating migration; EWI; group exposure
sources.Typical Data Captured: Rating; PD; watchlist; covenant; risk appetite; exposure
sources.Key Data Quality Controls: Temporal alignment; rating scale mapping; approved status

sources.Primary Relationship Coverage: Legal name; directors; filings; registered address; ownership where available
sources.Typical Data Captured: Company number; status; officers; filings; address; ownership
sources.Key Data Quality Controls: Jurisdiction coverage; update lag; entity matching
sources.Licensing / Privacy / Access Considerati: Access, licensing and permitted-use differ by jurisdiction

sources.Primary Relationship Coverage: LEI identity; direct and ultimate parent
sources.Typical Data Captured: LEI; legal name; status; parent relationships; exceptions
sources.Key Data Quality Controls: LEI status; parent exceptions; name/address match
sources.Licensing / Privacy / Access Considerati: Observe GLEIF terms and bank usage policy

sources.Typical Data Captured: Ownership %; corporate family; officers; financials
sources.Key Data Quality Controls: Coverage; update date; conflict resolution; source lineage
sources.Notes: Probable source listed in solution brief.

sources.Typical Data Captured: D-U-N-S; hierarchy; industry; address; trade relationships
sources.Key Data Quality Controls: Entity match; hierarchy confidence; coverage
sources.Notes: Useful for corporate identity and networks.

sources.Primary Relationship Coverage: Ownership; market risk; debt; corporate events; supply chain depending on product
sources.Typical Data Captured: Shareholders; securities; spreads; events; corporate hierarchy
sources.Key Data Quality Controls: Instrument-to-entity mapping; timestamp; product coverage
sources.Notes: Actual coverage depends on subscribed products.

sources.Typical Data Captured: Person; board role; appointment dates; company
sources.Key Data Quality Controls: Person disambiguation; active tenure

sources.Typical Data Captured: Importer/exporter; shipment; port; carrier; commodity
sources.Key Data Quality Controls: Entity matching; shipment duplication; coverage bias
sources.Notes: Useful for demo and sector-specific analysis.

sources.Primary Relationship Coverage: PE / VC sponsor; funds; portfolio companies
sources.Typical Data Captured: Sponsor; fund; investment; board rights; dates
sources.Key Data Quality Controls: Current holding status; sponsor/fund hierarchy

sources.Source / System: Reuters / Factiva / Court Filings / ESG Providers
sources.Typical Data Captured: Article/document; entities; event; jurisdiction; date; severity
sources.Key Data Quality Controls: Entity resolution; source credibility; duplicate events
sources.Notes: Essential for EWI and evidence-backed explanations.

sources.Source / System: IMF / OECD / World Bank / Central Banks
sources.Typical Data Captured: GDP; inflation; rates; country/sector indicators
sources.Key Data Quality Controls: Vintage; geography; scenario consistency
sources.Notes: Enriches stress scenarios rather than direct entity relationships.
